This workload accesses local memory (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#device-memory-accesses), accounting for 0.57% of all sectors requested in L1TEX. Local memory refers to a memory space that is private to each thread. Although it is logically distinct, local memory resides in global memory. This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
Some of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers), accounting for 88.73% of the local memory load (LDL) and 97.06% of the local store (STL) instructions. 29.75% of all local loads and 38.60% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 0.01% of all sectors requested in L2.
One common reason for the use of local memory is arrays being too large to fit into registers or not being indexed using compile time constants (see the Local Memory" section of the CUDA Programming Guide (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#device-memory-accesses). For more advice on how to reduce the usage of local memory refer to the documentation (https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/ProfilingGuide/index.html#metrics-hw-memory)."
